risk: Kinetic strike on central operations, HQ or hosting facility

risk: Third-party / vendor access compromise (supply-chain entry)
evidence: [Certain] Every major Gulf O&G intrusion entered through a third party: Petro Rabigh 2017 (misconfigured vendor-adjacent firewall), Bapco 2019 (VPN flaw), Aramco 2021 (1 TB leaked from contractors incl. risk: State-sponsored destructive OT/IT attack (wiper, SIS manipulation)
evidence: [Certain] Shamoon 2012 (30,000 PCs), Shamoon 2 2016–17, Triton 2017 (Triconex SIS, two ESD trips), Dustman 2019. No confirmed NOC OT disruption 2018–2026.

[Certain] Google Gemini not available in Oman (Jul 2026).

evidence: [Likely] Kuwait FY2025/26 deficit KWD 7.1 bn (15% of GDP), oil revenue −30%. [Certain] Aramco Q3 2026 capex ~$10.5 bn vs ~$12.6 bn y/y. [Certain] Wood Mackenzie (Nov 2026): NOCs face more competing demands on capital and management attention. Brent swung $70–$118 in 2026.

evidence: [Certain] Iraq accumulated arrears to contractors and IOCs during Hormuz closure; [Likely] BOC could default on GGIP phase-one payments (MEED, May 2026); Korean contractors owed ~$755 M at Karbala; Lukoil WQ-2 staff unpaid 6 weeks. No MENA energy AI incident on record.
